Prevention: Prepare land well by burning or burying volunteer cassava plants more than 50cm deep
Avoid planting cassava on the same piece of land for more than three years
Use clean, uninfested cassava planting material
Plant early in the rainy season to allow the plant to establish before the dry season to enable the plants to tolerate mealybug infection
Plant in fertile soil or improve the fertility (68 kg
O/ha) by using manure (2kg/m 2 ) or fertilisers to improve general health
Practise crop rotation with maize or legumes
Restrict movement of infested planting materials across borders
Monitoring: Regular visits to the farm at least fortnightly to look for signs and symptoms of the mealybugs
Observe shoot tips, leaves and stems for white waxy material
Look out for shoot tips with "bunchy tops" Look out for the presence of sooty moulds on shoots, tips, leaves and stems
Look for the presence of ants which feed on the honeydew secreted by the mealybug
Look out for curlings of the margins of leaves
Look for complete defolation of the cassava plant
P. manihoti is enough to start an outbreak so apply a direct control as soon as it is observed.
Direct Control: Remove and destroy infested plants or plant parts at early stages of infestation
Prune stems or leaves with high infestation and burn or bury more than 50 cm deep
Mix 5g of soap (alata samina) + 5g of powdered pepper in 1 liter of water and allow to stay for about 30 minutes.
Pour the mixture into knapsack and apply in 15 litres of water
Add 10ml soap to 1litre of water and stir to mix.
Add 50ml neem oil to the 1 litre water-soap solution and mix thouroughly.
Add the oil- water-soap solution to 14ltr water in the knapsack and apply within 8hrs.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
Pesticide use is not recommended for this pest because they destroy the natural enemies
When infestation is severe, apply chlorpyrifos ethyl 480g/l (e.g. rainchlopyr, Farin 200EC).
Apply 20mls/15l knapsack as full coverage and repeat when necessary.
Do not enter treated areas within 4hrs after application, PHI is 7 days; highly toxic to fish and aquatic organisms do not spray near waterways
